task_instruction:
Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi, I'm having trouble sending MMS messages. It's been a few hours now — texts send fine, but anything with a picture just won't go through.

turns.thought: I can help you get picture messaging working again. First, I need to pull up your account — could you confirm your phone number, or your full name and date of birth?
turns.execution_output: User: Sure, it's John Smith, and my number is 555-123-2002.

turns.thought: Thanks — let me look up your account.
Thanks, John. Let me look at your lines to find the one with that number.

Found it — your number 555-123-2002 is on line L1002 (Premium Plan, 15 GB), and you've used **15.1 GB of your 15 GB** allowance this cycle.

That's very likely the whole problem: once the plan's data limit is hit, data connectivity is cut off, and MMS requires mobile data even though regular SMS rides on the cellular connection alone — which is exactly why plain texts still go through but pictures don't.

Two ways to fix it:

- **Refuel data** — $2.00 per GB on your plan, up to 2 GB. Since your cycle ends 2025-02-28, a small top-up would comfortably cover the next few days.
- **Move to a plan with more data** — better value if you're regularly running up against 15 GB.

Everything else on the line looks healthy (status Active, contract good through 2026-12-31, roaming already on), so no suspension or billing issue is involved.

If you want to refuel, how much would you like — 1 GB ($2.00) or 2 GB ($4.00)? Once you confirm, I'll apply it and then walk you through a couple of quick checks on the phone to confirm picture messaging is working again.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, that makes sense — I didn't realize I'd blown through my data. Let's go with the 2 GB refuel, please. I'd rather not change my plan.
{"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}

turns.thought:
The 2 GB refuel went through — $4.00 added to your bill, and your line now shows 2.0 GB of refueled data on top of the 15 GB plan allowance.

Now let's confirm picture messaging is actually working. On your phone, please run through these:

1. **Check your status bar** — you should see a signal indicator and a network type like 5G/4G. If Airplane Mode is on, turn it off.
2. **Run a speed test** — it should no longer come back "no connection."
3. **Try sending the picture message again.**

If it still won't send, tell me what the status bar shows and the result of the speed test, and we'll dig into the next likely causes (network mode, APN settings, Wi-Fi Calling, or the messaging app's permissions).

One thing worth flagging: you're already at 15.1 GB with a week left in your cycle (it resets 2025-02-28). If this keeps happening, switching to a higher-data plan would almost certainly cost less month over month than refueling 2 GB at a time — happy to walk you through the options whenever you'd like.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check those things on my phone now.

turns.thought: Let me check the device on that line before we go further.

Thanks — that's helpful. Two separate things are showing up, and we need to clear both.

**1. Mobile data is switched off on the phone.** The "Data Disabled" indicator is just the phone's main mobile-data toggle, independent of your line's data allowance. Please turn it on:

> **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network → toggle Mobile data ON** (or swipe down and tap the signal/cellular tile).

Once it's on, run the speed test again.

**2. "No Signal" means the phone isn't seeing the cellular network at all** — so let's check the SIM. Your device is a Smartphone Pro Max (activated 2025-02-15, eSIM capable, last SIM/eSIM transfer 2025-01-20), so a seating or recognition issue is plausible:

> **Settings → About phone → Status → SIM status** (or **Settings → Network & Internet → SIMs**) and tell me what it reports — **Active**, **Missing**, or **Locked** (PIN/PUK).

Also worth noting: if your status bar shows a network type at all (5G/4G/3G/2G), tell me which one — MMS won't work on 2G.

Please do those two things and report back what you see. If the SIM shows "Missing," we'll reseat it; if it's "Locked," I'll need to get a specialist involved since that's a security matter. If it's "Active" but there's still no signal, we'll move on to network mode and APN settings.

That's the real culprit — with no SIM detected, the phone can't register on the network at all, which is why you have no signal, why mobile data won't enable (the toggle has nothing to connect through), and why MMS won't send. The data refuel I applied is still on your line and will be there once we get the phone connected — no data was wasted.

Please reseat the SIM card:

1. Power the phone **off** completely.
2. Locate the SIM tray on the edge of the device and eject it using the SIM eject tool (or a small paperclip).
3. Take the SIM card out and check that it's sitting flat and clean — wipe the gold contacts gently with a dry, soft cloth.
4. Put it back into the tray in the correct orientation, fully seated, and push the tray firmly back in until it clicks flush.
5. Power the phone back on.

Once it's back on, check the status bar and tell me what you see. If it now shows signal bars and a network type (5G/4G), then make sure mobile data is on and try the picture message again.

One note on your device: it's eSIM capable, and its last SIM/eSIM transfer was 2025-01-20 — so if you're actually using an eSIM profile rather than a physical card, tell me and we'll take a different approach, since there's no physical card to reseat.

Let me know how it goes.

Excellent — the SIM was the root of the connection problem. Signal, 5G, and mobile data are all back, so the prerequisites for MMS are in place. Since pictures still won't send, let's work through the MMS-specific causes. Please do these in order:

**1. Confirm data is actually flowing**
> Run a speed test on the phone. It should now return a speed rather than "no connection." If it comes back with anything at all, data is fine and we move on.

**2. Check your APN settings (most common MMS cause)**
> **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network → Access Point Names (APN)**
> Look at the **MMSC** field. If it's blank or doesn't look like a proper URL, that's your problem — MMS is routed through that server and won't send without it.
>
> If it's missing/incorrect: use **Reset to default** (the menu option in the APN screen), then **restart the phone** — the reset won't take effect until after a reboot.

**3. Check Wi-Fi Calling**
> **Settings → Network & Internet → Wi-Fi Calling**
> If it's **ON**, turn it OFF. Some configurations block MMS from going out over cellular while Wi-Fi Calling is active.

**4. Check the messaging app's permissions**
> **Settings → Apps → Messaging → Permissions**
> Make sure **Storage** (or Photos and videos) and **SMS** are both **Allowed**. Without storage access the app can't attach the picture at all.

After each step, try sending the picture message again. Most of the time it's the APN/MMSC setting.

Tell me what you find at step 2 — specifically whether the MMSC field is filled in — and what the speed test reported. If we get through all four and it's still failing, I'll bring in a technical specialist to go deeper.

That absolutely matters — being in France is very likely the reason data still shows "No Connection," and it's not something I could have guessed from the status bar alone. Good thing you mentioned it.

Here's the good news: I've confirmed on your account that **line L1002 is already roaming-enabled** (no change needed on our side, and enabling it is free). So the line is provisioned correctly for France.

The piece that's probably still off is the **Data Roaming toggle on the phone itself**. It's a separate switch from the mobile data switch, and when it's off the phone will happily show 5G and a roaming network in the status bar but refuse to pass any data — which matches your symptoms exactly.

> **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile network** (on some devices: **SIMs**) → toggle **Data roaming** / **Roaming** **ON**.
>
> Your phone may show a warning about roaming charges — accept it, since your line is already provisioned.

Then:
1. Run the **speed test** again — it should now return a speed instead of "No Connection."
2. Once data is flowing, **try the picture message** again.

On the frustration — that's completely fair, and I want to be straight with you: the SIM reseat wasn't wasted effort, since without a detected SIM you'd have had no service at all even on roaming. It's just that roaming was a second, separate problem stacked on top of it. Also worth noting the 2 GB refuel is applied to your line and hasn't gone anywhere.

If data roaming is already on, or turning it on doesn't fix the data connection, we'll go one more step and check the network mode preference and VPN status — and if we still can't get data flowing abroad, I'll get you to a roaming technical specialist rather than keep putting you through steps.

Let me know what the toggle was set to and what the speed test says after.

Great progress — that confirms the no-data problem was purely the phone's roaming toggle. Your line itself is fully in order: Active, roaming-enabled, 2 GB refueled, contract good through 2026-12-31, no billing or suspension issues. So everything from this point is device-side.

Since data is now flowing at 275 Mbps and your APN has a valid MMSC URL and Wi-Fi Calling is off, the next thing to check is the **messaging app's permissions** — without storage access it physically can't attach the photo, and it will fail at send even with perfect connectivity.

> **Settings → Apps → Messaging (or Messages) → Permissions**
>
> Make sure **Storage** (may be labeled "Photos and videos") and **SMS** are both set to **Allow**. If either is set to "Don't allow," switch it to Allow.

Then try sending the picture message again.

Report back what those two permissions were set to and whether it sent. If they were already allowed (or granting them doesn't help), the two remaining checks are your **network mode preference** and **VPN status** — and if those come back clean, I won't keep putting you through hoops. At that point the most likely explanation is an MMS-over-roaming limitation on the visited network in France, which needs a roaming technical specialist to work through with your carrier's roaming partner, and I'll transfer you to a human agent to take that on.

You're welcome — glad we got there. In the end it took three separate fixes, each clearing a different blocker:

1. **Reseating the SIM** — the phone had no SIM detected, which meant no network registration, no signal, and no way for mobile data to come up at all.
2. **Turning on data roaming** — you're in France, and the phone's roaming switch was off, so it showed 5G but passed no data. Your line was already roaming-enabled on our side; this was the device toggle.
3. **Granting the messaging app storage and SMS permissions** — it couldn't attach or send the picture without them.

Two notes for your records:

- The **2 GB refuel ($4.00)** has been applied to line L1002 and will appear on your bill. It stays on the line until your cycle resets on **2025-02-28**, so you've got it available for the rest of this cycle.
- Since data is working while abroad now, keep **data roaming on** for the rest of your trip — turning it off will bring back exactly the "connected but no data" state you saw earlier.

If picture messaging gives you any more trouble, or you'd like to look at higher-data plan options before your next cycle starts, just reach out.
turns.execution_output:
User: Will do — I'll leave data roaming on for the rest of the trip. Thanks again for the help, that's everything I needed.
